title: Anna's virtues that the tomb cannot hide
english: Her character was dignified, her grace humane, and her manner obedient toward her parents, for reverence led her as a great teacher standing by. The splendid marks of her lineage shone in her, and her steadfast love of husband against nature, which by the force of widowhood shakes what is unsteady, yet in the struggle defeated by stronger powers, from which the bright garlands shine in a manner worthy of one married to one husband: the boldness of Anna.

title: The tomb cannot darken Anna's lesson
english: The tomb will not be able to darken these things. For the beautiful mouth that carries a lesson for life could never escape notice. And if it should, the inscription placed beside the tomb itself will speak more than all.

orientation: Arethas is concluding his praise of Anna, arguing that her grave cannot hide the virtue her life taught.

title: Febronia's compassion remembered even among the dead
english: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men, did something with tokens of her compassion, if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor. For not even there do the souls of the great-hearted forget their beneficence to the uttermost. Yet may the span of our life be sufficient to send her on to the divine bridal chamber of Christ—she, as a reverend bride, took hold of the lamp of purity, keeping it bright with the oil of love for the poor. Know that this is the sign of her long sleep.
